request: Analyze GSE277623 for PMID 42318351 (Empagliflozin-pirfenidone dual therapy improves cardiac function and structure in a preclinical two-hit HFpEF model.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (DNBSEQ-T7, BGI) of rat left ventricle, male rats only, n = 3 per group (one EMPA and one PFD sample excluded for corrupted files -> 19 samples)
final.intervention: pharmacological: empagliflozin (0.35 g/kg/d), pirfenidone (0.3 g/kg/d), or both, by oral gavage for 4 weeks after 5 weeks of L-NAME + high-fat diet (S3.1.p1-p2). Exercise appears only as an outcome readout (treadmill exhaustion test, S3.5.p1), never as an intervention or a sequenced group.
final.primary_estimand: Transcriptional effect of EMPA + PFD dual therapy versus untreated (PBS vehicle) HFpEF in rat left ventricle (S4.4.p1, S4.4.p4 'TE'). No exercise estimand exists in the paper.
planned_contrasts: EMPA+PFD vs untreated 9w (TE; S4.4.p1: 717 DEGs, 421 up / 296 down)
EMPA+PFD / PFD / EMPA / untreated vs HFpEF 5w (S4.4.p2: 2954 / 1492 / 439 / 439 DEGs)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (independent animals, one LV sample each)

paper_threshold.source_locator: S3.9.p1; FIG5 legend (adjusted p < 0.05 and absolute fold change > 2)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The paper (S3.1.p1-p2) is a drug-treatment study in a two-hit HFpEF rat model. The RNA-seq groups (S3.9.p1, S4.4.p1-p4, FIG5) are control/HFpEF at 5 weeks and control/untreated/EMPA/PFD/EMPA+PFD at 9 weeks. The only exercise element is a treadmill exhaustion test used to measure exercise tolerance as a functional endpoint (S3.5.p1, S4.1.p4); no group was exercise-trained and no sequenced sample is defined by exercise.

checks: Data availability S11.p1 and S3.9.p1 name GSE277623
GEO series: Rattus norvegicus heart, male, RNA-Seq, htseq-count, rn6 (matches S3.9.p1)
19 samples = 7 groups x 3 minus the 2 excluded monotherapy samples (S4.4.p1): EMPA n=2, PFD n=2

_RAW.tar members are GSM-prefixed per-sample htseq-count files (GSM8526569_Con_5W_1 ... GSM8526587_EMPA_PFD_9W_3), giving an exact GSM key; the series-level GSE277623_raw_count.txt.gz carries the same labels without GSM ids

ownership.reasoning: The accession, organism, tissue, sex, pipeline and sample counts all match the paper. The per-sample tar is used because its file names carry GSM ids, which allows exact alignment instead of decoding label abbreviations.

grp: ^Heart, (control|HFpEF|untreated|EMPA treated|PFD treated|EMPA and PFD treated) ([59]) weeks, biorep \d+$

alignment.reasoning: Tar columns are GSM ids, matching the metadata index exactly. grp is derived from the GEO title (group + week), cross-checked against characteristics 'disease state', 'time' and 'treatment'.

final.paper_input: htseq-count raw counts into DESeq2 via iDEP (S3.9.p1)

matrix.reasoning: All values are integers (inspect: integer_fraction 1.0, max 329596); GEO data_processing and S3.9.p1 state HISAT2 + htseq-count, i.e. raw read counts, the input the paper fed to DESeq2.

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: every sequenced group is defined by disease induction (L-NAME + HFD), time point, or drug treatment (EMPA, PFD, EMPA+PFD, PBS vehicle). Exercise appears only as a treadmill exhaustion test used as a functional outcome (S3.5.p1, S4.1.p4); no animal was exercise-trained, so the data cannot identify an effect of exercise on gene expression.

candidates.value: grp EMPAPFD9W vs PBS9W (paper's primary TE contrast)
candidates.reason_rejected: drug-treatment effect, not an exercise effect; outside the request's estimand
disease or age effects; no group differs by exercise exposure

design.reasoning: S3.1.p1-p2 and S4.4.p1-p4 define seven groups by disease, time and drug; none by exercise. The treadmill test in S3.5.p1 measures exercise capacity as an endpoint and is not a sequenced factor. Refused at design.

discrepancies.paper: drug-treatment study (EMPA, PFD, EMPA+PFD vs vehicle in HFpEF rats); exercise only as a treadmill tolerance endpoint
discrepancies.data: 19 LV samples in 7 groups defined by disease/time/drug; no exercise factor
